## Notes

- **`DECIMAL_RE` loses its anchors (`^…$`)** — Unanchored, `1,499 USD` and `$499` start parsing as numbers — the surface that must stay unknown becomes a value two producers can be stamped against.
- **`parseSurface` returns `{tag:"number", payload: trimmed}` for any unmatched surface — the raw-surface collapse** — The mutation the suite exists for: it destroys the abstain band without failing any test that merely asserts a successful parse.
- **`canonicalCurrency` drops the `ISO_4217` membership test (back to any three letters)** — Every three-letter unit token (`mos`, `yrs`, `kgs`, `net`, `min`) becomes a currency, and two spellings of one quantity read as provably different.
- **`canonicalInstant` loses its calendar round-trip** — `new Date` rolls an impossible calendar day forward rather than refusing it, so `2026-02-31T10:00:00Z` becomes byte-identical to a real neighbouring day.
- **`canonicalDate` loses its calendar round-trip** — `Date.UTC` normalizes rather than rejecting — without the round-trip `2026-02-31` and `2026-03-03` compare EQUAL.
- **a declaration OVERRIDES the surface instead of narrowing it** — The four payload-free kinds may only ever CONFIRM the surface. Overriding lets a producer declaration re-label a date as a number. The docstring this table replaced carried 3; two independent spellings of the mutation (re-tagging from the declaration, and simply dropping the `parsed.tag === declared.kind` narrowing) both measure 4, so that cell was stale rather than ambiguous.
- **`comparableValueWithReason` collapses `declaration-rejected` into `abstained`** — Both return sites, because collapsing only one leaves the other still reporting the distinction — which is not what the label says. Measured: both sites 3, the final return alone 2. The docstring this table replaced carried 2 without recording which spelling it meant, and that ambiguity is the whole reason the spelling is now the input rather than a description of it.
- **`comparableValue` prefers the surface parse over `entityId`** — Demotes the entity store below the parser, so a resolved `Enterprise tier` / `Enterprise Plan` pair stops comparing equal the moment either surface happens to parse.
- **`comparableDifferentSql` loses its `split_part` tag equality arm** — Whatever dies here is LEXICAL — the SQL-arms assertion at the bottom of the suite — because `agree` is the TypeScript twin and deleting a SQL arm does not touch it. The behavioural falsifiers live in `identity-consumers-pg.test.ts` and `object-cmp-pg.test.ts`.
- **`comparableDifferentSql` loses its known-tag `IN` arm** — Covered behaviourally by `object-cmp-pg.test.ts`'s unknown-tag test, not here.
- **`comparableDifferentSql` loses its `strpos(…) > 0` separator arms** — Both arms together — they are one guard. `split_part` returns the WHOLE STRING for a separator-less value, so without them the six bare tag names read as provably different from every real value of their own type. Covered behaviourally in `object-cmp-pg.test.ts`.
